podcast.body: He wrote this song, which was the first single from *Rumours*, reaching the top 20 and securing the #120 spot on *Rolling Stone*'s "500 greatest songs of all time." The lyrics explicitly addressed his turbulent relationship with Stevie Nicks during the band's internal conflicts. "Go your own way was actually the first single from rumors and it made it to made it into the top 20 and it's also on that rolling stone list at clocks in at 120."

podcast.body: Written by Lindsey Buckingham, this song reached number 10 on the charts. It was Buckingham's response to Stevie Nicks, featuring lyrics accusing her of "packing up and shacking up" and expressing her "yearning for freedom." "In return, Lindsay wrote the number 10 hit Go Your Own Way about Stevie's own yearning for freedom, accusing her of packing up and shacking up."
